You are coding NSW motor accident decisions for a research dataset. Read the decision text supplied and assign each ordinal score from the text alone.

Score each dimension INDEPENDENTLY. A decision describing a severe case will score high on some dimensions and not others: severe physical injury does not by itself imply a contested proceeding, a disputed liability, or a prominent psychological component. Judge each scale against its own definition and resist letting an overall impression of severity carry across the scales.

If the text does not support a judgement on a dimension, give the lowest score rather than guessing upward, and say so in `uncertain`.

DECISION TEXT:
--- Catchwords ---
MOTOR ACCIDENTS -

Motor Accident Injuries Act 2017 ; assessment of damages pursuant to sections 7.36(3) and 7.36 (4); non-economic loss; injuries included tibial fracture requiring surgery, aggravation to degenerative cervical spine changes, bilateral subacromial subdeltoid bursitis, and rotator cuff tears; ongoing neck, shoulders and knee pain; Held – past economic loss ($209,478.18); future economic loss ($745,095); partial retained earning capacity $400 weekly considered and increased vicissitudes 20%; heavier type roles would cease before age 67 years.

--- Key Paragraphs ---
[para 47] Records claimant’s current age and ongoing symptomatology relevant to NEL.
47. The claimant is presently aged 49 years old. He continues to suffer pain on a daily basis. He is unable to undertake any further treatment to alleviate some of his symptoms as he has a hereditary blood clotting disorder which is life threatening with surgery.

[para 51] States the current statutory maximum for non-economic loss anchoring the assessment.
51. The current maximum amount for non-economic loss from 1 October 2025 is $691,000.

[para 59] Determines and quantifies non-economic loss at 370,000.
59. Noting the claimant's age and the extent of the continued impact from injuries for the remainder of his life, I assess non-economic loss in the sum of $370,000. Economic loss

Past economic loss

[para 89] Finds pre-injury weekly earnings/net basis, underpinning past loss.
89. I am satisfied on the evidence before me that the claimant was exhibiting a pre-injury earning capacity of $1,498 net per week at the time of the subject accident.

[para 108] Totals past economic loss including superannuation and Fox v Wood.
108. I assess past economic loss inclusive of weekly losses, tax and superannuation in the sum of $209,478.18 representing weekly losses in total of $172,438 plus $18,968.18 (superannuation) plus $18,072 (tax). Future economic loss

Claimant's submissions

[para 121] Sets out the statutory framework for future economic loss (ss 4.7 and 4.9).
121. The relevant sections governing awards in respect of future economic loss include ss 4.7 and 4.9 of the Act. Section 4.7(1) of the Act states that damages may not be awarded for future economic loss unless the claimant first satisfies the court or claims assessor that the assumptions about future earning capacity or other events on which the award is to be based, accord with the claimant's most likely future circumstances but for the injury.

Section 4.7(2) of the Act provides that the amount of damages for future economic loss that would have been sustained on those assumptions is to be adjusted by reference to the percentage possibility that the events concerned might have occurred but for the injury.

Section 4.7(3) of the Act provides that if an award for future economic loss is made, the court or Commission is required to state the assumptions on which the award was based and the relevant percentage by which damages were adjusted.

Section 4.9(1) of the Act provides that where an award of damages is to include compensation, assessed as a lump sum, in respect of damages for future economic loss which is referrable to deprivation or impairment of earning capacity, the present value of the future economic loss is to be qualified by adopting the prescribed discount rate.

Section 4.9(2) of the Act prescribes a discount rate of 5%.

[para 137] Finds retained earning capacity of 400 weekly.
137. I consider the claimant has a retained earning capacity which is limited by the hours he could possibly work and the roles he is fit for. The estimated retained earning capacity of $400 submitted by the claimant is an appropriate residual earning capacity. Noting the claimant has attempted to work and is willing to seek other roles and continues to do so, his evidence that he is trying to look for suitable roles is accepted as genuine.

[para 140] Performs the core future loss calculation, including multiplier and vicissitudes.
140. I allow losses as follows: $1300 net x 625 (18 years multiplier 5% tables) = $812,500 (less 20 % vicissitudes $162,500) = $650,000.

[para 142] States the total future economic loss figure.
142.

I assess the claimant's future economic loss in the total sum of $745,095. Assessment of damages summary

[para 144] Summarises total damages assessed under s 7.36.
144. I assess the claim as follows on the findings set out above:

Non-economic loss $370,000 Economic losses

Past economic losses $209,478.18

Future economic losses $745,095 Total of economic losses and non-economic loss $1,324,573.18

Total damages assessed $1,324,573.18
